objective: Repair the missing Adaptive Metareasoning Governor runtime surface referenced by BOOTSTRAP and prevent piecemeal optimization of an existing integrated system before checking whether the desired mechanism already exists end-to-end.

roles_before.artifact: BOOTSTRAP.md routes nontrivial reasoning through PROTOCOL.md and explicitly says to use its Adaptive Metareasoning Governor, but current PROTOCOL.md has no such section.
PROTOCOL.md keeps reasoning proportional and stops when more analysis cannot materially change the decision.
BOOTSTRAP.md + PROTOCOL.md route current state through exact owners/live owners and forbid stale-memory substitution.
PROTOCOL.md + references/architecture-change-contract.md require candidate isolation, preservation, adversarial tests and verified promotion for architecture changes.
tests/system_model_regression.md already covers context economy, research treadmill, lifecycle boundary and local-patch failure classes, but lacks an explicit existing-system gap-first probe.
Git history contains the pre-lean Adaptive Metareasoning Governor, including decision grounding, best-so-far and bounded-depth semantics.

role_dispositions.destination: Restore a compact actual Adaptive Metareasoning Governor section in PROTOCOL.md that requires gap-first breadth before depth for optimization/diagnosis of existing systems.
Keep the existing total-value and Stop rules; the restored governor is only two runtime lines plus a heading.
Gap-first inspection uses the same exact owners/live owners; no authority or mutable-state ownership changes.
This repair itself follows Architecture Mode and does not loosen any write/mutation gate.
Add one explicit Case Y for the piecemeal existing-system trap and pin it through the already-executed continuity guard.
Keep the pre-lean governor recoverable in Git history and preserve this manifest as failure lineage.

capability_probes.assertion: A tiny self-contained reversible task must still be answered directly without broad architecture inventory or ceremonial metareasoning.

When asked to optimize an existing integrated XMind/Ron OS/System behavior, the assistant must inspect the smallest end-to-end existing mechanism set needed to test whether the gap already exists before proposing a restructure, new rule or new bridge.
Current facts still come from exact owners/live sources and live-source mutations still require their existing exact permissions.
The fuller pre-lean Adaptive Metareasoning Governor and the reason for this compact restoration remain recoverable from Git history and this manifest.

tests.expected: PASS only when BOOTSTRAP's Adaptive Metareasoning Governor reference resolves to a concrete PROTOCOL section and Case Y pins the existing-system gap-first failure class.

tests.command: python3 tests/architecture_change_guard.py && python3 tests/architecture_change_guard_selftest.py && python3 tests/continuity_coverage_guard.py && python3 tests/continuity_coverage_guard_selftest.py
tests.expected: PASS with owner/live authority, XMind permission boundaries, lean Stop behavior, domain routing and prior regression anchors preserved.

preflight_notes: The failure is not absence of all metareasoning evidence: tests/system_model_regression.md already contains adjacent cases. The runtime defect is that BOOTSTRAP names an Adaptive Metareasoning Governor that current PROTOCOL.md no longer contains after lean compaction.
The repair intentionally restores only a compact two-line runtime rule instead of re-expanding the historical long governor.
